question: How much should a window dim when a child opens in front of it, so the window in front leads while the way back stays readable?
criteria: The front window is clearly the one you are working in; the windows behind it don't pull your eye.
The titles behind are still easy to read, so you can see where you came from and how to go back.
The stack reads as one set of glass layers in depth, not as separate cards pasted on top of each other.
Nothing looks dirty or muddy: a dimmed window still looks like the same glass, just further back.

fixtures.note: The real Catalog from src/ through demo/bench.html, three levels deep, from the front and from 35 degrees to the side. distanceM 0.6 is the locked bubble reference distance. Values here are scene setup, never tokens.
